subject: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — prioritization and bridge call
messages:
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com; compliance@medverity.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — incoming asks from MedVerity

Team — looping you all in on a MedVerity request that just came through their CISO. High level: they need longer retention of audit logs (7 years for certain records), evidence packaging for SOC-style reviews, and a BYOK/KMS carveout for encryption keys. Attachments: MedVerity-evidence-request.pdf + a quick retention spreadsheet (retention-proposal-v1.xlsx).

What I need from each function to triage:
- Security (Neha): quick assessment of compliance gaps & risk surface if we offer longer retention/BYOK exceptions.
- Infra/Product (Karthik): feasibility and high-level dev effort (phases) — both for an interim export flow and for per-tenant KMS.
- Legal/Customer ops (Laura): contract/terms ask and whether a carveout is feasible without a new SLA.
- Sales (Ben): commercial sensitivity and deal impact / timeline expectations.

Proposed next steps: 1) Brief triage notes by EOD, 2) 30-min bridge call tomorrow to align owners and a timeline we can give MedVerity.

Background/context: This is an enterprise expansion request on top of the existing Dedicated trial; they flagged regulatory requirements for long-term retention and control over keys. They prefer Redwood to host if we can demonstrate audited export and tenant-key isolation.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com; compliance@medverity.com
Date: 2026-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — incoming asks from MedVerity

Thanks Marcus — initial triage below. Attached: security-impact-notes.txt (short list).

Summary of asks and immediate risks:
- 7-year retention: feasible from a storage perspective but increases attack surface and must be paired with immutable storage and WORM policies for evidence integrity.
- BYOK/KMS per-tenant: requires KMS integration plus key lifecycle and escrow/rotation policies; operational complexity increases (key custody, key compromise playbooks).
- Evidence packaging: we can provide time-bounded export bundles (signed) but will need a documented attestation process for audits.

Blocking dependencies:
- KMS integration (cloud KMS + optional HSM routing) — effort from infra & ops.
- Audit export pipeline (immutable storage & signing) — infra + storage budget.
- Legal sign-off on exception language (Laura).

Risk-level: medium-high if we accept BYOK without hardened controls and SOC evidence. Short-term mitigations:
- Offer an export + signed bundles flow (customer-run retrieval) as a stopgap.
- Deny BYOK for certain data classes until we've validated HSM/escrow approach.

I'll add owners to the security tickets and can be on the bridge call.

— Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — incoming asks from MedVerity

On Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 09:12, marcus_lin@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — looping you all in on a MedVerity request that just came through their CISO...

Quick feasibility notes from infra/product perspective:
- Short term (2–4 wk): export & signed-bundle workflow that pulls relevant audit logs into a GCS/S3 bucket and provides per-export checksums + simple retention metadata. Low risk, low effort (~1.5 engs for 3 weeks).
- Mid term (2–3 mo): tenant-level retention policy + server-side lifecycle rules and support for longer on-cold storage (Glacier/Archive). Requires storage config, billing changes, retention UI, and policy enforcement (~2–3 engs).
- Longer term (4–6 mo): optional BYOK per-tenant with KMS integration and HSM-backed keys. High effort: key management surface area, rotation, backup escrow, and support for legal hold. Estimate: ~4 engs + 1 SRE + security review cycles.

Technical constraints & questions:
- Does MedVerity require us to hold their KMS keys in an HSM under their control, or just be willing to accept keys they supply?
- Are they asking to exclude certain event classes from standard retention policies? (We need exact scope.)

I'll create a JIRA ticket and attach the infra estimates; happy to walk through on the bridge call.

— Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — incoming asks from MedVerity

Appreciate the fast triage so far. Product prioritization input:
- Short-term (export + signed bundles) = must-have for enterprise. Low lift and buys time.
- Mid-term (retention tiers + lifecycle) = high value for multiple customers; mark P1 for Q4 work queue but split into two sprints.
- BYOK/HSM = P2 for now; we'll accept an exceptions process only if legal and security sign off and we can scope minimal viable BYOK (no escrow first).

Please prepare for a 30-minute bridge call tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to align owners: agenda below. I've created a shared folder with the MedVerity packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-compliance-retention

Proposed bridge call agenda (30 mins):
- 5m: Quick ask summary (Marcus)
- 10m: Security & infra risk/mechanism (Neha + Karthik)
- 5m: Legal constraints & suggested contract language (Laura)
- 5m: Commercial ask & timeline commitments (Ben)
- 5m: Agree owners + next steps

Laura/Ben: please confirm if the exception needs an interim commercial credit or new SLA to fast-track.

— Evelyn Hart
VP, Product (Platform)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Audit log retention & BYOK exception — incoming asks from MedVerity

Hi Evelyn/Team — thanks for the quick response and proposed cadence. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Retention: the 7-year request applies to authentication and admin audit logs only; application-level logs can be shorter.
- BYOK: MedVerity wants control over encryption keys (they'd prefer keys to be customer-held in HSM) but understand a phased approach.
- Evidence: the export bundle should include signed checksums and a simple index mapping event types to retention class.

Attached: MedVerity-req-sheet.docx (detailed columnar requirements). Can you confirm if backups and snapshots are in scope for the 7-year retention?

Thanks —
Chiara R.
Head of Compliance, MedVerity
